newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU vets Sanofi/Bristol-Myers joint venture.
newsitem.headline: EU vets Sanofi/Bristol-Myers joint venture.

text.p: The European Commission said on Monday it had started a routine probe into a joint venture between Bristol-Myers Squibb of the United States and Elf Aquitaine's subsidiary Sanofi to pool forces in the market for cardiovascular medications.

The two pharmaceutical giants have jointly developed a new drug called Clopidogrel to prevent the risk of ischemic stroke, myocardial infarction and vascular death in patients with a history of symptomatic atherosclerotic disease.
They have also developed Irbesartan to treat hypertension.

The Commission said in a statement published in the EU's Official Journal that the joint venture was submitted for clearance earlier this month under EU rules which ban practices restrictive of fair competition or abuse of dominant position.
It called on interested parties to file comments within 10 days. There is no deadline for the Commission to take a decision.
The two partners have also filed their new drugs for marketing registration on the European and U.S. markets.
